summary: A 1933 Aermotor fire tower in the Pinaleno Mountains, inactive since the 2017 Frye Fire; sources disagree on whether the tower survived.

facts.design: 46-foot Aermotor tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab (register: MC-40; hiking club: CL 100-106)
facts.status_note: Inactive. The 2017 Frye Fire destroyed the support structures, and the condition of the cab is uncertain.

visit.trail_note: Trail head sign at Columbine Campground; the trail is hard to follow in places because of fallen timber and erosion

corrections.why: The register and the hiking club both give the tower as 46 feet, about 14.0 m; 13.7 m is about 45 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2020 register visit and the hiking club both describe a standing steel frame after the Frye Fire. The Weebly lookout site says the tower was destroyed. This story reports the Weebly claim as disputed rather than adopting it.
The register gives 9,984 ft (3,043 m) and the hiking club gives 10,029 feet. Both are cited; neither is treated as settled.
The register names an Aermotor MC-40 and the hiking club names a CL 100-106. Both are reported in the story, not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Tower fate is disputed. The Weebly page says it was destroyed; the 2020 NHLR visit and the GVRHC hiking-club report both describe a standing steel frame. The story reports the dispute. Height: the record gives 13.7 m, but both the register and the hiking club give 46 feet (about 14.0 m); a correction is proposed. Model (MC-40 vs CL 100-106) and elevation (9,984 vs 10,029 ft) are unresolved and both are reported. The Living New Deal page and the NARA nomination PDF returned 403, so the NRHP nomination text itself was not read; the CCC architect claim comes from the NPGallery record. Staffing and the trail note are from the May 2020 register visit only, not checked since. The GVRHC PDF publisher name is taken from the domain and was not confirmed from the document. Read budget: seven read attempts, one over the six-read cap (two of the attempts were 403 errors).
